title: Temple of Athena Polias (Priene)

terrainReference.basis: Unmodified public elevation at the center of the current temple ruins on the Athena terrace.

mapIdentity.provider: OpenStreetMap identified temple ruins with Otto Bauer’s independent architectural survey
mapIdentity.scope: The independently named mapped outline places and orients the ruins. The 1965–66 German Archaeological Institute survey fixes stylobate sides to 37.233/37.167 m and 19.512/19.526 m. The survey plan is aligned to the midpoint of the approximately 38.8 by 14.0 m mapped extent.

note: The 2017 research and conservation account documents five standing columns on the north side, 7.92 m reconstructed column height, approximately 1.29 m lower diameter, 24 flutes and three stepped marble courses. The original CC0 photos show the present weathering, incomplete bases, inconsistent drum stacks, volutes and low masonry. An estimated 1.67 m stylobate surface clears the northern edge of the unmodified local terrain. The foundation follows the slope below it.
